notice-er26-3515-1110.point: FERC notices PJM's compliance filing on the Large Load definition and registry, filed November 9 with comments due November 30, 2026.
notice-er26-3515-1110.quote: Compliance filing: Compliance Filing re Large Load Definition and Large Load Registry to be effective 10/12/2026.

notice-er26-3515-1110.point: FERC notices PJM's new Section 205 filing revising the backstop procurement rules from ER26-3380, effective January 29, 2027.
notice-er26-3515-1110.quote: §205(d) Rate Filing: Revised Reliability Backstop Procurement Rules in ER26-3380-000 to be effective 1/29/2027.

notice-er26-3515-1110.point: Interventions and protests are due by 5:00 pm Eastern on each comment date.
notice-er26-3515-1110.quote: must file in accordance with Rules 211, 214, or 206 of the Commission’s Regulations (18 CFR 385.211, 385.214, or 385.206) on or before 5:00 pm Eastern time on the specified comment date.

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: The Counsel says the order lets PJM exclude state consumer advocate offices from the registry's confidential information.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: that order allows PJM to exclude state consumer advocate offices from the list of entities entitled to access confidential information to be collected and maintained in the Large Load Registry.

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: It says advocates need data on large load magnitude, location and growth to test cost shifting to consumers.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: Responsibility for advocating for consumer interests cannot be meaningfully discharged without access to information concerning the magnitude, location, and anticipated growth of large load.

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: It argues confidentiality can be handled by protective measures rather than categorical exclusion.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: Legitimate confidentiality and security concerns can be addressed through protective measures rather than categorical exclusion.

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: The Counsel cites the Market Monitor's figure of $29 billion in added capacity costs over four auctions.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: data center growth has driven $29 billion in additional capacity costs over the last four Base Residual Auctions

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: It lists three errors: no reasoned decision, undue discrimination versus state commissions, and inconsistency with the show cause rulings.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: Whether FERC’s ruling excluding state consumer advocate offices from the confidential information in the Large Load Registry is inconsistent with its rulings in the Show Cause proceedings

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: The June PJM show cause order found cost information lacking for state regulators, which the Counsel says supports advocate access.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: makes it difficult for interested parties, including transmission customers and state regulators, to accurately assess which transmission costs are driven by requests for transmission service

rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.point: The Counsel asks FERC to direct PJM to extend registry access to consumer advocates.
rehearing-er26-3515-ohio.quote: FERC should reverse its ruling on this issue, and direct PJM to extend access to the Large Load Registry confidential information to state consumer advocate offices, subject to confidentiality obligations.

compliance-er26-3515-pjm.point: PJM drops the two registry fields tied to its rejected capacity proposal.
compliance-er26-3515-pjm.quote: the amount of BYONC brought by a particular Large Load and the allocated RBP UCAP MW quantity

compliance-er26-3515-pjm.point: A Large Load is 50 MW of cumulative peak at one electrical site.
compliance-er26-3515-pjm.quote: a cumulative peak load of 50 megawatts or greater at a single electrical site behind one or more points of interconnection

compliance-er26-3515-pjm.point: Loads in service before June 1, 2027 must be reported by March 1, 2027.
compliance-er26-3515-pjm.quote: prior to June 1, 2027, shall provide the information required by RAA, Schedule 11.B.1 to the Office of the Interconnection by March 1, 2027.

compliance-er26-3515-pjm.point: Later loads must be reported before they enter service.
compliance-er26-3515-pjm.quote: before the in-service date of the Large Load.

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC accepts the Large Load definition and registry as severable, effective October 12, 2026, and orders compliance within 30 days.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: we accept PJM’s proposed Tariff revisions to establish a definition of Large Load and a Large Load Registry, effective October 12, 2026, as requested, and require PJM to submit a compliance filing within 30 days

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC finds the 50 MW threshold balances visibility into larger loads against excluding smaller ones.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: establishing the threshold to qualify as a Large Load at a cumulative peak of 50 MW strikes a just and reasonable balance

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC keeps manufacturing and other load types in the Large Load definition alongside data centers.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: we find reasonable PJM’s proposal to include all types of large loads in the Large Load definition.

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC treats the remaining elements as an integrated package and rejects them together.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: the only elements of its proposal that are severable are the proposed definition of Large Load and the proposed Large Load Registry

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: IRAS appears to intrude on retail rate regulation beyond FERC's Section 205 authority.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: certain aspects of PJM’s proposal appear to present an impermissible intrusion on retail rate regulation and are not subject to the Commission’s authority pursuant to section 205 of the FPA.

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: PJM did not support treating distributors differently based on retail customer characteristics.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: PJM did not adequately support its proposal to treat Electric Distributors and LSEs differently based on the characteristics of their retail customers.

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC flags that curtailing firm load at EEA1 may conflict with mandatory Reliability Standard EOP-011-4.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: It appears that PJM’s proposal ignores the plain language of mandatory Reliability Standard EOP-011-4

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: FERC suggests non-firm service like Non-Firm Contract Demand as an avenue for a refiling, citing the E-7 flexible-load directive.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: a non-firm transmission service similar to Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service, with appropriate adjustments, might be considered as a potential avenue to achieve some of the aims of PJM’s proposed IRAS framework.

order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.point: Commissioner Rosner concurs, saying a refiling must justify curtailing IRAS load before voluntary demand response.
order-er26-3515-pjm-large-load.quote: it must justify its proposal to curtail IRAS load on a mandatory basis before load that has voluntarily enrolled in a demand response program.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM says the 2027/2028 auction fell short of the reliability requirement and calls IRAS and the registry the needed tools.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: The Base Residual Auction for the 2027/2028 Delivery Year procured insufficient capacity to meet the PJM Region Reliability Requirement.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: Absent new capacity, PJM says new large loads must be flexible and reduce demand during emergencies.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: Absent such new capacity, New Large Loads must be flexible and, pursuant to PJM’s operational needs, reduce their energy demands when called upon during system emergencies.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM says it offered severable elements and urges timely approval of the registry, definition and bring-new-capacity obligation.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: PJM highlights the importance of timely Commission approval of the following discrete elements: the Large Load Registry,

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM cites a July 22 event in which nearly 4,000 MW of data center load tripped offline in Virginia.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: a July 22 event saw nearly 4,000 MW of data center load trip offline unexpectedly in Virginia. It was the largest such event in PJM history.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM defends the 50 MW threshold as consistent with the June 2026 show cause order and rejects a baseline for existing loads.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: No information presented by any of these parties renders PJM’s proposed threshold unjust and unreasonable.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM argues IRAS directs only a MW quantity to distributors and leaves retail curtailment choices to states.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: it neither targets nor directs specific retail customers to be subject to curtailment, nor compels or restricts the authority of the retail authority to prioritize among the retail customers

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM asks FERC to prescribe changes or give guidance if it rejects any element.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: the Commission either direct prescriptive changes to be implemented on compliance or provide guidance to aid PJM and stakeholders to develop a just and reasonable approach.

pjm-september-iras-answer.point: PJM agrees to clarifying edits on compliance to the bring-your-own-capacity language for demand resources.
pjm-september-iras-answer.quote: PJM agrees that the “not” included in this section should be removed

filing-20260903-5199.point: DCC supports bring-your-own-generation and state interruptible tariffs but calls IRAS legally defective.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: DCC believes that the IRAS proposal is legally defective and must be rejected.

filing-20260903-5199.point: IRAS would compel states to conform retail curtailment rules to a PJM tariff, which DCC says disregards the federal-state division of authority.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: IRAS instead seeks to compel states within the PJM footprint to conform their retail curtailment frameworks to PJM tariff requirements.

filing-20260903-5199.point: DCC offers a state opt-in alternative in which states set interruptible classes and PJM signals curtailment under state tariffs.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: states would be responsible for establishing interruptible customer classes for large load customers while PJM would continue to monitor system conditions

filing-20260903-5199.point: Network service customers serving new large loads pay full capacity charges but are curtailed ahead of demand resources.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: PJM proposes to curtail these customers prior to deploying Demand Resources that have been committed to provide capacity to maintain reliability

filing-20260903-5199.point: Loads get under ten months to procure new capacity with no transition mechanism.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: effectively provides New Large Loads a window of less than ten months to procure new capacity or face curtailment

filing-20260903-5199.point: Excluding eligible new large loads from the Variable Resource Requirement curve from 2029/2030 would distort capacity prices.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: excluding Eligible New Large Loads from the calculation of the Variable Resource Requirement curve (“VRR Curve”) beginning with the 2029/2030 Delivery Year

filing-20260903-5199.point: Alternatively DCC asks for a Section 206 proceeding, a transition mechanism and an implementation delay to June 1, 2028.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: the Commission should direct PJM to delay implementation of IRAS until June 1, 2028

filing-20260903-5199.point: On jurisdiction, FERC may not approve tariff terms that set retail service terms or curtailment priority.
filing-20260903-5199.quote: FERC may not approve tariff provisions that directly regulate retail customers, dictate retail service terms, or prescribe the curtailment priority of retail customers.

filing-20260903-5212.point: The advocates cite the June 2026 show cause order's finding on PJM's tariff and ask FERC to require non-firm service for new large loads that do not self-supply.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: new large loads that do not self-supply must take non-firm transmission service.

filing-20260903-5212.point: They want only resources that have not cleared a prior Base Residual Auction to count as new capacity.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: only resources that have not previously cleared a prior Base Residual Auction (BRA) are eligible.

filing-20260903-5212.point: PJM's design lets a load reduce curtailment risk with capacity that already cleared, adding load without adding supply.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: This would increase the amount of load on the system without either increasing system supply or making the new load an IRAS resource subject to curtailment.

filing-20260903-5212.point: Compensating curtailed loads leaves states to decide who pays, so other customers may fund payments to data centers.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: which leaves open the possibility that non-large load customers may yet end up paying resource adequacy costs to the new large data center loads that are driving PJM’s reliability concerns.

filing-20260903-5212.point: The Market Monitor figures show data center demand raised costs to other customers by $23.1 billion over three auctions.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: The total increase in costs to other PJM customers as a result of data center load in the last three BRAs was $23,100,955,341.

filing-20260903-5212.point: FERC has called large loads a separate category and directed every RTO and ISO to define them.
IRAS could meet the roughly 6.8 GW need the backstop targets, sooner and more durably, making the backstop unnecessary.
filing-20260903-5212.quote: IRAS can satisfy the capacity need at which the RBP is aimed sooner, more durably, and, if correctly modified as non-firm transmission service, at less cost.

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI supports the registry and a wholesale curtailment signal before pre-emergency procedures, but not the compensation mechanism without clarification.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: the Commission should not accept PJM’s proposed compensation mechanism, without further clarification.

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI supports calling IRAS before pre-emergency load management so existing customers and demand response do not bear the first consequences of a shortfall.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: Calling on IRAS first appropriately places the initial operational consequences of a capacity shortfall on the amount of demand associated with NLLs that entered the system without sufficient new capacity

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI says differential treatment of new large loads should include less firm service.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: This differential treatment should reasonably include less firm service.

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI supports removing new large loads without their own capacity from the demand curve starting with the 2029/2030 auction.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: NLLs entering the system without sufficient new capacity should not be permitted to increase capacity-market demand and rely on PJM’s existing capacity supply to satisfy that incremental requirement.

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: States need meaningful registry access to design retail curtailment and cost allocation.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: states must have meaningful access to the Registry so they can determine how curtailment should be implemented at the retail level

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI asks PJM to clarify whether retail regulators can set the IRAS rate or only decide eligibility for compensation.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: PJM should clarify whether retail regulators can set the IRAS rate itself at retail or if they simply have the ability to determine whether specific retail loads are entitled to compensation

opsi-september-iras-comments.point: OPSI says the 50% rate is unsupported because PJM calls a zero rate just and reasonable.
opsi-september-iras-comments.quote: The Commission should sever and reject proposed Attachment DD-4 § X and accept the remainder of PJM’s filing without the unsupported 50% compensation mechanism

filing-20260903-5206.point: The PA PUC supports a New Large Load registry but objects to the compensation language in Appendix A.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: PA PUC supports the creation and maintenance of a New Large Load (NLL) Registry and suggests improvements to the Registry.

filing-20260903-5206.point: The tariff lets a large load accept less than 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate in retail rates, which the PA PUC says abdicates retail authority.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: retail ratemaking authority would be inappropriately and unlawfully abdicated to NLLs.

filing-20260903-5206.point: PJM's compensation ranges from 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate down to zero.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: PJM’s proposal also allows eligible NLLs to agree upon a retail rate between 50% of the Non- Performance Charge Rate and zero dollars

filing-20260903-5206.point: The PA PUC says the large load would effectively set its own curtailment compensation, with no validation of actual curtailment.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: Under this scheme, the NLL functions as a retail rate regulator that sets its own curtailment compensation rates up to a maximum threshold of 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate.

filing-20260903-5206.point: It cites Pennsylvania Executive Order 2026-05 limiting data center costs on other customers.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: Governor Josh Shapiro signed Executive Order 2026-05 on August 18, 2026.

filing-20260903-5206.point: Alternative language sets compensation at 0% unless a state regulator permits up to 50%.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: The rate for the provision of Interim Resource Adequacy Service shall be 0% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate

filing-20260903-5206.point: State commissions should have access to the registry and to curtailment data.
filing-20260903-5206.quote: state utility commissions should have access to the Registry and curtailment data should be provided in the Registry.

filing-20260901-5028.point: The PA PUC joins OPSI's request to move the deadline from September 3 to September 14, 2026.
filing-20260901-5028.quote: PA PUC supports and joins in OPSI’s request that the Commission extend the time for comments in this docket from September 3, 2026 to September 14, 2026.

filing-20260901-5028.point: The PA PUC finds ambiguity between PJM's transmittal letter and tariff redlines on a 0-50% compensation range.
filing-20260901-5028.quote: We find some ambiguity due to discrepancies between PJM’s transmittal letter and the red-lined

filing-20260901-5028.point: The curtailment protocol may intrude on state jurisdiction over retail rates.
filing-20260901-5028.quote: The curtailment protocol was not developed with PA PUC’s input, and it may impinge upon our jurisdiction over retail rates.

filing-20260901-5028.point: The tariff does not recognize state authority to prohibit, approve or modify distributor compensation and recovery.
filing-20260901-5028.quote: The tariff does not expressly recognize state authority to prohibit, approve, or modify such compensation and jurisdictional recovery.

filing-20260828-5287.point: OPSI asks to move comments from September 3 to September 14, 2026, and PJM does not oppose.
filing-20260828-5287.quote: OPSI requests that the Commission extend the time for comments in this docket from September 3, 2026 to September 14, 2026.

filing-20260828-5287.point: PJM's August 13 filing proposes a load reduction service for new large loads and a large load registry.
filing-20260828-5287.quote: a new supplemental capacity product through which New Large Loads [(“NLL”)] provide a load reduction service that is a tool available to PJM to manage resource adequacy shortfalls

filing-20260828-5287.point: PJM's compensation mechanism creates new obligations for Electric Distributors and touches retail ratemaking.
filing-20260828-5287.quote: PJM proposes a compensation mechanism for loads that provide this new service, which creates new obligations for Electric Distributors.

filing-20260828-5287.point: State regulators need time to assess the interaction of PJM, distributors and retail regulators in implementing the service.
filing-20260828-5287.quote: to allow the retail regulators in the PJM region additional time to consider the complex interaction between the rights and responsibilities of PJM, Electric Distributors, and retail regulators

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: IRAS lets PJM prioritize load reduction in zones where new large loads brought no capacity of their own, and only in real-time shortage conditions.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: a service to be implemented by PJM solely during periods when there are insufficient resources to reliably meet demand in real time operations.

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: New large loads avoid IRAS by bringing new capacity, and PJM ties the design to SPP's CHILLS and the June show cause orders.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: This principle lays the foundation for the IRAS paradigm in PJM that facilitates large load interconnections in a manner similar to the Southwest Power Pool’s (“SPP”) Conditional High Impact Large Load Service

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: A Large Load is defined as 50 MW or more of cumulative peak load at a single electrical site, with affiliated facilities within one mile combined.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: cumulative peak load of 50 megawatts [(“MW”)] or greater at a single electrical site behind one or more points of interconnection

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: PJM would direct each distributor zone to cut load up to the MW tied to eligible new large loads, and states choose which load to reduce.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: each Electric Distributor zone/area may be directed by PJM dispatchers to reduce load up to the MW quantity of capacity attributable to Eligible New Large Loads in that zone/area.

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: Compensation for load reduction is capped at 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate—as the maximum rate for IRAS performance.

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: From 2029/2030 PJM would exclude new large loads without bring-your-own-capacity arrangements from the demand curve.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: exclude from the VRR Curve New Large Loads, to the extent they do not have arrangements with sufficient BYONC, beginning with the 2029/2030 Delivery Year.

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: PJM proposes no end date for IRAS.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: not proposing an end date to the IRAS program.

filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.point: PJM requests an October 12, 2026 effective date for the revisions and registry, with IRAS available from June 1, 2027.
filing-er26-3515-pjm-iras.quote: make the enclosed proposed Tariff and RAA revisions effective by no later than October 12, 2026
